name: athletedata.health
why: Proactive AI endurance coach (Telegram/WhatsApp) that reads WHOOP/Oura recovery and Garmin Body Battery each morning and swaps sessions on low recovery; the developer posts on the Slowtwitch and Intervals.icu forums. Recovery-first product built on other brands' gated APIs.
why_now: Covered by the5krunner 30 Apr 2026; active developer forum threads
channel: Developer forum thread (Intervals.icu / Slowtwitch) or site
opportunity: Add Vybe as a direct morning-recovery source (overnight HRV/RHR) beside WHOOP/Oura/Body Battery; DevKit loan for their coach logic
unknowns: No public partner contact; user numbers are self-reported (8000+); pricing not confirmed
ask: DevKit loan and a 15-min call on adding Vybe as a recovery source
opener: Your coach reads WHOOP, Oura and Body Battery every morning, which is exactly the data we produce. We're building Vybe, a screenless ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK and API, and picking 5-10 DevKit design partners. Would you want to test a direct overnight HRV feed in athletedata? Happy to send a unit.

name: Funraisin
why: Peer-to-peer fundraising platform with fitness-challenge tracker integrations. Its support page says it cannot reliably support Fitbit after Google's API change, that existing Fitbit connections stop working, and points fundraisers to Garmin, Strava or MapMyFitness instead.
why_now: Fitbit integration dropped for the Fitbit Web API sunset (Google support ended 30 Sep 2026; shutoff 30 Oct 2026)
ask: Intro call: would a no-subscription band with an open API be a useful tracker option for charity challenges after Fitbit
opener: Saw Funraisin's note that the Fitbit integration can't continue after Google's API change. We're building Vybe, a screenless wearable with a licensed SDK/API and no subscription, launching to consumers May 2027. Would a new tracker option with a direct API be useful for your fitness-challenge clients? Glad to share the DevKit docs.

name: Aduro
why: Employee wellbeing platform. Its support article says new Fitbit connections are turned off and existing ones stop syncing after 28 Sep 2026, routing users through Google Health to Apple Health/Health Connect instead of a direct device feed.
ask: Intro call on adding Vybe as a direct device for employer programs in 2027
opener: Saw Aduro's notice about turning off direct Fitbit connections. We're building Vybe, a screenless band with a licensed SDK and API and no subscription, consumer launch May 2027. If a device with a direct feed would help your employer programs, could we compare notes for 15 minutes?

name: HRV Flow
why: Apple Watch recovery-score app (wake-up HRV, RHR and sleep to a 0-100 score). The founder's Product Hunt comment says they built it because a daily recovery score required paying WHOOP or Oura subscriptions; asks for feedback from users who tried them.
ask: Feedback swap: test Vybe DevKit as a no-subscription overnight source for their score
opener: Your HRV Flow launch note about not wanting to pay WHOOP or Oura monthly just for a recovery score is why we're building Vybe: a screenless ECG/HRV band, no subscription, with a licensed SDK/API. We're picking 5-10 DevKit design partners. Want to try feeding your score from it?

name: AlphaHRV
why: Garmin Connect IQ data field that computes DFA alpha1 from chest-strap RR intervals; Intervals.icu plots alpha1 only from this field. Users report accuracy depends heavily on the strap (Polar H10 recommended), i.e. the product is bottlenecked on beat-to-beat hardware.
ask: Feedback: would raw ECG-derived RR from the Vybe DevKit be useful for alpha1 validation
opener: Following the AlphaHRV threads on Intervals.icu, the strap quality issue keeps coming up. We're building Vybe, a screenless ECG band with a licensed SDK that exposes RR data, and picking 5-10 DevKit design partners. Would ECG-derived RR be useful for your alpha1 work? Happy to send a unit.

name: IntervalsWellnessSync
why: Indie iOS app that pulls sleep, HRV, resting HR, SpO2 and weight from HealthKit into Intervals.icu wellness; HRV/RHR come only from sleep sessions. A small builder piping overnight recovery data, a natural early tester for a new HRV source.
ask: Feedback on the Vybe DevKit API vs HealthKit for overnight HRV sync
opener: Saw IntervalsWellnessSync on the Intervals.icu forum. We're building Vybe, a screenless ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK and API, and want feedback from people already moving overnight HRV into training tools. Would you try a DevKit and tell us where our API is worse than HealthKit?

name: Watchletic
why: Watch app that sends HRV, sleep duration and resting HR to Intervals.icu; newly released on Wear OS. Indie builder working on overnight recovery data across watch platforms.
why_now: Wear OS version newly released (2026 forum thread)
ask: Feedback on Vybe DevKit API as an extra HRV/RHR source
opener: Saw Watchletic's Wear OS release on the Intervals.icu forum. We're building Vybe, a screenless ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK and API, and picking 5-10 DevKit design partners. If an overnight HRV/RHR feed beside the watch is interesting, could we talk for 15 minutes?

name: Intervals.icu Open API and app ecosystem

Is there a preferred way to get listed as an app integration, and would a DevKit post on the forum be welcome?

name: Gadgetbridge
why: Open-source, cloud-free Android companion app for wearables. Publishes a 'New gadget tutorial' for adding devices, says contributions are welcome, and its release notes say adding a device is hard without the hardware, so owners who test are valued. Releases in 2026 (0.90-0.92) keep adding devices and Health Connect support.

ask: Open an issue offering DevKit units and BLE protocol docs to a maintainer willing to add Vybe support
opener: Hi Gadgetbridge team. We're building Vybe, a screenless ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK, and we'd rather document our BLE protocol than make anyone reverse engineer it. Would a maintainer be interested in DevKit hardware plus protocol docs to add Vybe support? Happy to follow your contributor policy.

name: Stanford Spezi (SpeziBluetooth / SpeziDevices)
why: Open-source Swift framework for digital-health apps; SpeziBluetooth models BLE devices declaratively and SpeziDevices ships reusable device implementations (Omron BP cuff and scale) with pairing and measurement processing. The team says anyone can contribute modules; good-first-issues are listed.

opener: Hi Spezi team. We're building Vybe, a screenless ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK, and we'd like research apps built on Spezi to use it without custom glue. Would you welcome a SpeziDevices module for the Vybe DevKit, alongside the Omron implementations? We can provide hardware for testing.

why: Open-source mHealth research platform (King's College London / Maudsley BRC) whose Android passive app uses per-device plugins on a shared commons API; integrations wiki lists device plugins and a REST connector for web-API wearables.

name: python-garminconnect / Home Assistant Garmin Connect
why: Popular Python Garmin Connect wrapper (about 2.2k stars reported) and the HACS Home Assistant custom integration built on it, which exists because Garmin removed API access for hobby projects. 2026 issues show logins breaking after Garmin SSO/MFA changes; its users want self-hosted health data.
